chunks: 5 - He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Muhalabi narrated to us, said: Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Asad al-Isfahani narrated to us, said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, said: Muhammad ibn Ali informed us, said: al-Husayn ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Jahdham al-Azdi, from his father -- who was from the people of Sham -- who said:

When Uthman expelled Abu Dharr from Madinah to Syria, he used to preach to us, praising God, testifying to the truth, and invoking blessings upon the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, and would say: To proceed -- indeed, we were in our age of ignorance before the Book was revealed to us and the Messenger was sent among us, yet we fulfilled our promises, were truthful in speech, kind to our neighbours, hospitable to guests, comforted the poor, and despised the arrogant. And when God, the Most High, sent among us His Messenger, peace be upon him and his progeny, and revealed to us His Book, those moral qualities were pleasing to God and His Messenger, and the people of Islam were more worthy of them and more fitting to preserve them. They remained upon that for as long as God willed.

Then the rulers have introduced evil deeds that we did not know: a Prophetic tradition being extinguished, and an innovation being revived; a speaker of truth being called a liar; selfishness without piety; and a trustworthy one from among the righteous being deprived. O God, if what is with You is better for me, then take me to Yourself without my having changed or altered.

He used to repeat these words and proclaim them openly. Then Habib ibn Maslamah came to Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and said: Abu Dharr is corrupting the people against you by saying such and such. So Mu'awiyah wrote to Uthman about it, and Uthman replied: Send him back to me. When he arrived in Madinah, he exiled him to al-Rabdhah.

key_terms.أثرة: Atharah - selfishness, hoarding of wealth without piety, a key grievance of Abu Dharr
key_terms.الربذة: Al-Rabdhah - a desolate village near Madinah where Abu Dharr was exiled and died in poverty
key_terms.بدعة: Bid'ah - religious innovation, contrasted with the extinguishing of sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.جاهلية: Jahiliyyah - the pre-Islamic age of ignorance, here cited by Abu Dharr to contrast with the moral decline he witnesses under the current rulers

ai.seo_question: Why was Abu Dharr exiled to al-Rabdhah and what did he preach about in Syria?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the exile of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, a prominent companion of the Prophet known for his outspoken criticism of corruption and wealth hoarding among the rulers. After Uthman sent him from Madinah to Syria, Abu Dharr publicly preached about the moral virtues the Arabs possessed even before Islam, which Islam then endorsed, and how the rulers had since abandoned those values in favor of innovation and injustice. His speeches prompted Mu'awiyah to complain to Uthman, who ordered Abu Dharr sent back and ultimately exiled him to the desolate outpost of al-Rabdhah.
